metadata.name: ADAPTIVE POLICIES — Adaptive execution strategy
metadata.purpose: Optimize the balance between quality and token consumption according to the user story's complexity

principio_rector.formula: Sophistication proportional to the user story's complexity
principio_rector.regla: Do not run the entire machinery for trivial user stories
Do not sacrifice quality on complex user stories

clasificacion_complejidad.descripcion: The Orchestrator classifies each user story into 4 levels

ejemplos.ejemplo: Fix a typo in a message

estrategia.accion: DO NOT load: shared contract, full standards, V1/V2 validation

caracteristicas.item: No impact on an existing contract

ejemplos.ejemplo: Add a field to a form (backend already exists)
New GET endpoint without complex logic

estrategia.accion: DO NOT load: Exhaustive performance, SEO, a11y policies (unless the user story requires it)
Load: Relevant policies (security, transactions, error handling)
DO NOT load: Policies that do not apply (e.g. SEO if a private page)

caracteristicas.item: Architectural impact or impact on multiple modules

ejemplos.ejemplo: Shopping cart (products, inventory, calculation, persistence, notification)
Auth migration (change from JWT to OAuth with backward compatibility)

estrategia.accion: Orchestrator: Exhaustive analysis + complete contract + critical structures
Load: ALL relevant policies (security, performance, a11y, SEO, concurrency, external integrations)
Integrator: Exhaustive E2E validation (functional, security, UX, a11y, performance)

politica.name: Transactions
politica.condicion: If the user story modifies multiple tables/entities

politica.name: Concurrency
politica.condicion: If the user story has read-modify-write operations or inventory

politica.name: Performance
politica.condicion: If the user story is complex OR explicitly requires optimization

politica.name: Security
politica.condicion: If the user story involves AuthN, AuthZ, sensitive data

politica.name: A11y (WCAG)
politica.condicion: If the user story creates/modifies public UI

politica.name: SEO
politica.condicion: If the user story creates/modifies public pages

politica.name: External integrations
politica.condicion: If the user story calls external APIs (payments, email, etc.)

politica.name: Files & uploads
politica.condicion: If the user story handles file uploads

politica.name: Backward compatibility
politica.condicion: If the user story modifies public APIs

politica.name: Git workflow
politica.condicion: If the request mentions branches, commits, or push (git-workflow.xml)

politica.name: Containers and environment
politica.condicion: If running the system or delivering it operable is requested (engineering-standards.xml)

politica.name: Validation scripts
politica.condicion: If there is real integration or E2E (engineering-standards.xml, scripts)

formula_decision.descripcion: Complexity calculation based on quantifiable factors
formula_decision.formula:
Complexity = (Files modified × 1) + (Business logic × 3) + (Transactions × 5) + (External integrations × 5) + (Impact on contracts × 4) + (Explicit quality requirements × 2)
If Complexity < 5 → TRIVIAL If Complexity 5-15 → SIMPLE If Complexity 16-35 → MODERATE If Complexity > 35 → COMPLEX

factores_de_elevacion.descripcion: The quantitative formula is a floor, not a ceiling. These factors raise the level by at least one step and set validation minimums
factores_de_elevacion.factor: Loads seguridad_aplicacion; complete V1/V2; Integrator mandatory; negative security tests
Forbids sensitive values in logs, responses, and fixtures; secret scanning mandatory
Complete shared contract and Backend-Frontend identity verification
Migration tested from scratch and against the real engine
project-modes.xml protocol, environment and containers, exhaustive validation

modo_lote.descripcion: When the request contains several user stories (epic)
modo_lote.regla: A single project analysis and one epic contract; the context cost is amortized across user stories.
Per-user-story complexity to decide each specialist's depth; the batch inherits the highest for the Integrator and the cross-cutting gates.
Execution in dependency order; each user story is closed (green tests + commit according to git-workflow.xml) before starting the next one that depends on it.
The Integrator runs once per batch with the real stack and walks through all user stories; findings are corrected together.
Batch token budget: sum per user story + fixed overhead of analysis and integration; the validation level is not reduced because of batch size.

reglas_ejecucion.regla: The Orchestrator always runs (analyzes the user story, classifies complexity and routing, decides policies, generates handoffs)
Specialists according to complexity: - TRIVIAL: 1 specialist - SIMPLE: 1-2 specialists - MODERATE/COMPLEX: 2-3 agents + Integrator
Integrator according to complexity: - TRIVIAL: NO - SIMPLE: Only if FULL_STACK - MODERATE: If FULL_STACK - COMPLEX: Always
Proportional validation: - TRIVIAL: Change review only - SIMPLE: Light V1 + V2 tests - MODERATE: V1 + V2 + complete tests - COMPLEX: V1 + V2 + tests + E2E + evidence

User stories with impact on security/critical data
User stories that modify public contracts/APIs

Academic projects that require traceability and evidence
